card text: In an alternator the rotor makes the magnetic field; the stator windings produce the output current.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Alternator output is controlled by the?
card text: An alternator needs only a voltage regulator; diodes stop reverse current, and it limits its own current.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Automobile starter motors are?
card text: Starter motors are series-wound DC motors.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: 'Dwell' is?
answer: Time (cam angle) the contact points stay closed
card text: Dwell (cam angle) is the angle through which the contact breaker points stay closed.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: A spark plug with a white insulator tip shows?
card text: A white or blistered spark plug tip means overheating — e.g. over-advanced timing, lean mixture or too hot a plug.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: How many ignition coils in a distributorless ignition (DLI) system for a six-cylinder engine?
card text: A wasted-spark DLI uses one coil for each pair of cylinders: 6 cylinders → 3 coils.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a rotating-armature magneto, the magnet is?
card text: In a rotating-armature magneto, the armature rotates between fixed permanent magnets.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Which is NOT part of the chassis?
card text: Chassis = frame, suspension, steering, brakes, wheels, axles and power train. Electrical system and body are not chassis.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In four-wheel drive there are?
card text: In 4-wheel drive both front and rear axles are live (driven) axles — two live axles.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Front suspension must: support weight; keep control in hard braking; move pinion up; keep steering control and alignment. Which are correct?
card text: Front suspension supports front weight, keeps control in hard braking and keeps steering control and wheel alignment.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: A MacPherson strut combines the shock absorber with a?
card text: A MacPherson strut has the shock absorber inside a coil spring as one unit.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Most widely used steering gearbox in passenger cars?
card text: Rack and pinion steering is the most common in cars.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Front wheels closer at the front than at the rear (at rest) is called?
card text: Toe-in: front wheels are closer together at the front than at the back.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: What does ABS need to work?
card text: ABS uses wheel speed sensors to detect a wheel about to lock and then reduces its brake pressure.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Braking force at the vehicle's centre of gravity is the product of?
card text: Maximum braking force = coefficient of friction (tyre-road) × vehicle weight.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a master cylinder, the primary piston is the one that is?
answer: Pushed directly by the push rod
card text: The primary piston is pushed directly by the pedal push rod; the secondary piston moves by fluid pressure.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a friction clutch, the flywheel lies between the?
card text: In a clutch, the flywheel (on the engine crankshaft, the driving shaft) is one friction face; the clutch plate on the gearbox input (driven) shaft presses against it.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a gear set, speed reduction means torque increase, and torque increase means speed reduction. Which is correct?
card text: In gears, power stays (almost) the same, so lower speed means higher torque, and higher torque means lower speed.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Which epicyclic gear condition gives reverse?
answer: Sun drives, ring driven, carrier held
card text: Epicyclic gear: holding the planet carrier gives reverse — the ring turns opposite to the sun.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: A propeller shaft absorbs the change in drive angle (axle moving up and down) with?
card text: Universal joints take care of changes in drive angle; the slip joint takes care of changes in length.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: The hole in the rim for the tyre valve is called?
card text: The hole in the wheel rim for the inflation valve is the valve aperture.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: An under-inflated tyre wears most?
card text: Under-inflation wears the tread edges (shoulders); over-inflation wears the centre.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: An essential requirement of an EV battery is?
card text: EV batteries need high energy density (range) and high power density (acceleration), long life and safety.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In an SI engine, pre-ignition means the fuel ignites?
card text: Pre-ignition: the mixture ignites before the spark, from a hot spot.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Which statement about normal SI combustion is NOT correct?
answer: Peak pressure at the end of after-burning
card text: In normal SI combustion, peak pressure comes soon after TDC during flame propagation — not at the end of after-burning.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Which statement about diesel knock is incorrect?
answer: Chance decreases as ignition delay increases
card text: Diesel knock gets WORSE with longer ignition delay — more fuel collects and burns all at once.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a CI engine, the phase from maximum pressure to maximum temperature is?
card text: CI combustion: ignition delay → rapid combustion → controlled combustion (from peak pressure to peak temperature) → after-burning.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: A limitation of supercharging is?
card text: Supercharging increases mechanical and thermal load on engine parts — that is its limitation.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Match: heat engine, refrigerator, internal energy, reversibility with friction loss, Kelvin-Planck, Clausius, point function.
card text: Heat engine → Kelvin-Planck; refrigerator → Clausius; internal energy → point (state) function; friction makes processes irreversible.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: A closed system gets 130 kJ heat and does 165 kJ work. Change in internal energy?
card text: First law: ΔU = Q − W = 130 − 165 = −35 kJ (internal energy falls).

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: For the same compression ratio, which is true?
card text: For the same compression ratio, the Otto cycle is more efficient than the Diesel cycle.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a two-stage reciprocating compressor, total work is minimum when?
card text: Two-stage compressor work is minimum when both stages do equal work — pressure ratio per stage = √(P3/P1), with perfect intercooling.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Correct: BMEP = ηm × IMEP; ITE < BTE; Morse test gives IP; 2-stroke power half of 4-stroke?
card text: BMEP = mechanical efficiency × IMEP, and the Morse test gives indicated power. Indicated thermal efficiency is higher than brake thermal efficiency.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Brake power 120 kW, fuel 15 kg/h. Brake specific fuel consumption?
card text: BSFC = fuel per hour ÷ brake power = 15 ÷ 120 = 0.125 kg/kWh.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Chapter XII of the MV Act, 1988 deals with?
card text: MV Act Chapter XII = Claims Tribunals (MACT). Chapter XI = insurance against third-party risks. Chapter VIII = control of traffic.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Legal blood alcohol limit for drivers in India?
card text: Section 185: driving with more than 30 mg alcohol per 100 ml of blood (breath test) is an offence.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: A car pulls to one side on braking though brakes are fine. Reason 1: wrong toe. Reason 2: worn control-arm bushing.
card text: Pull during braking with good brakes can come from wrong toe setting or worn control-arm bushings.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Which are correct: carriageway includes shoulder; right of way is up to road land boundary; right of way is between building lines; shoulder is for stopped vehicles and lateral support?
card text: Right of way = total land width acquired for the road (up to road boundary). Shoulders give room for stopped vehicles and side support. Carriageway excludes shoulders.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Design of road gradient and sight distance depends mainly on?
answer: All: traffic volume, road surface and speed.
card text: Gradient and sight distance design depend on design speed, traffic volume and road surface (friction).

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: The clutch friction disc is splined to the?
card text: The clutch friction disc is splined to the gearbox input (primary) shaft, so it can slide but turns with it.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Body construction used in modern passenger cars?
card text: Modern cars use monocoque (frameless, unitary) construction — body and frame are one shell.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: In a traffic signal cycle, which phase follows amber?
card text: Signal order: green → amber → red. Amber warns that red is coming.

exam: Lecturer in Automobile Engineering (Govt. Polytechnics)
question: Excessive fuel consumption in a carburettor engine can be due to?
card text: A high float level makes the carburettor deliver too much fuel — rich mixture and high consumption.
